result.rationale: refreshOAuthTokens returns the raw fetch Response from CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, while consumers expect provider-specific shapes — e.g. Google's CalendarService does `const token = res?.data; googleCredentials.access_token = token.access_token` (an axios-shaped object), and HubSpot/Lark/Office365 consumers similarly do `response.json()`/SDK-shaped handling on the sync-path Response, which lacks `.data`. The sync path thus returns an object no consumer can parse, breaking token refresh whenever the sync endpoint is configured.

judged_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:3 — `refreshFunction: () => any` returns either a raw fetch `Response` (sync path) or whatever each provider callback returns (Google `res` with `.data`, HubSpot SDK camelCase token object, Lark `{code,data}` envelope Response, MS/Webex provider JSON), so there is no normalized token contract and no consumer's post-processing can accept the sync endpoint's "access token and expiry only" shape — enabling CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT breaks refresh for every integrated app (see per-app findings).
